# How EEG Machines Read Your Brain — 2D scientific motion graphics (code project)

**How scalp electrodes detect the electrical activity generated by the human brain.** A 55-second, 9:16, 60 fps,
seamless-loop explainer in premium flat-vector 2D motion graphics (Kurzgesagt-inspired, original drawings): an EEG
trace already scrolling at frame 0; the monitor and a patient wearing scalp electrodes; a layered cutaway into the
occipital cortex; a cortical network; pyramidal neurons with aligned apical dendrites; a synapse releasing transmitter;
ion channels opening; a postsynaptic potential with its sink and source; a synchronized population whose fields add
up; the field spreading through fluid, skull and scalp; the electrode array; one electrode on its gel; a differential
channel; the microvolt signal with mains hum and drift; the differential amplifier; common-mode rejection; filtering;
sampling into digital values; the multichannel recording; eyes-closed posterior alpha; eyes open and alpha fading; a
clinician reviewing the recording — and the camera settling back on the same O1 trace, which is frame 0.

No narration, no subtitles. On-screen text is small and secondary: the brief's five context labels (HOW EEG WORKS,
NEURONS, SCALP ELECTRODES, AMPLIFIER, ALPHA RHYTHM) plus, on request, nine very short explanatory captions
(ion currents · fields add up · spreads to the scalp · measures A − B · microvolts · shared noise cancels ·
sampled → digital · eyes open: alpha fades · voltage, not thoughts). The film reads without them.

| | |
|---|---|
| Video | 1080×1920, 60 fps, 3,300 frames (55.000 s), H.264 High, yuv420p, BT.709. Drawn as vectors on a Canvas 2D engine, so every frame is anti-aliased at full resolution (no pixel art, no 3D). |
| Audio | Original futuristic electronic score, 104.73 BPM, 24 bars = 55.000 s, F# minor, plus 111 SFX on the sixteenth-note grid of the score. AAC 256 kbit/s, 48 kHz stereo. Full mix −22.0 LUFS integrated, true peak −2.2 dBTP (a quiet bed for a later voiceover). |
| Loop | A true loop: frames 0…3299 are unique samples at t = f/60; frame 3299 is the moment just before frame 0. The waveform, the camera, the eyelids and every sound continue through the boundary. |

## Render it yourself

Requirements: **Node ≥ 18**, **ffmpeg** (libx264), **Python 3** with **numpy** and **scipy** (mastering), and
**[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)** for the picture (the skill's renderer runs headless Chromium through Playwright).
Once: `uv run --with playwright playwright install chromium`.

```
cd eeg_motion
node tools/export.js                      # everything: the picture once, then all four MP4 variants + three WAVs
```

That writes:

| File | Sound |
|---|---|
| `output/EEG_How_It_Works.mp4` | music + SFX |
| `output/EEG_How_It_Works_No_Music.mp4` | SFX only — no background music |
| `output/EEG_How_It_Works_No_SFX.mp4` | music only — no SFX |
| `output/EEG_How_It_Works_Silent.mp4` | no audio track (the audio-free master) |
| `output/audio/EEG_How_It_Works_Full_Mix.wav`, `…_Music_Only.wav`, `…_SFX_Only.wav` | 24-bit / 48 kHz stems |

Only one variant, or a few:
```
node tools/export.js --mix full           # EEG_How_It_Works.mp4 (music + SFX)
node tools/export.js --mix nobgm          # _No_Music (SFX only)
node tools/export.js --mix nosfx          # _No_SFX (music only)
node tools/export.js --mix silent         # _Silent (no audio)
node tools/export.js --mix nobgm,silent   # several, comma-separated
node tools/export.js --audio-only         # only the three WAVs
node tools/export.js --video-only         # only the silent picture build/video.mp4
node tools/export.js --rerender           # render the picture again even if build/video.mp4 is current
```
The picture is rendered **once** (about 10 frames per second, so roughly 6 minutes for 3,300 frames) and kept as
`build/video.mp4` with a fingerprint of the engine sources; another variant later only re-muxes it in seconds. The
three audio renders take about 15 s. If your installed Chromium needs a matching Playwright, set
`PW_PKG="playwright==<version>"`.

All audio versions are mastered with **one common gain** (the full mix at −22 LUFS), so the music-only and SFX-only
versions are exactly as loud as they sit in the mix (−24.0 and −25.4 LUFS on their own).

Preview without rendering: `cd engine && python3 -m http.server 8000`, open `http://localhost:8000/index.html`
(scrub and play; the preview is silent). Stills at chosen seconds:
`uv run --with playwright python engine/render.py --width 1080 --height 1920 --stills 0,12,30,45 --out build/stills`.

Check the loop (three repetitions, watch both joins at normal speed):
```
printf "file 'EEG_How_It_Works_Silent.mp4'\nfile 'EEG_How_It_Works_Silent.mp4'\nfile 'EEG_How_It_Works_Silent.mp4'\n" > output/loop3.txt
ffmpeg -f concat -safe 0 -i output/loop3.txt -c copy output/loop_check_3x.mp4
```

## The seamless loop

The film opens on the O1 trace (a posterior channel) already scrolling, the camera at rest in a close-up, and pulls
back from rest. It ends by settling on exactly that composition: the same world point, the same zoom, zero velocity on
both sides of the join. The trace is one signal: every component (alpha 9.6–10.4 Hz, background 1.3–28 Hz, hum, drift)
completes a whole number of cycles in 55 s, the scroll speed never changes, and the screen shows the last 10 s of that
periodic signal — so frame 3299 flows into frame 0. The patient's eyes start to relax at 51.9 s, are half closed
through the join and finish closing at 1.4 s; the posterior alpha envelope follows them, so the opening trace already
carries the rhythm. The score's bar 24 (C#7sus4) resolves into bar 1 (F#m9), a soft riser rings across the join into
the hook pulse, and every reverb and delay tail wraps.

Measured: on the proxy concatenated three times, the step across each join changes 12.0 % of the picture, the steps
just before it 12.9–13.3 % (the deliberate fast pull-back right after frame 0 then rises to 40 %). In the WAVs the
sample step across the join (0.019) is smaller than the median sample step within 50 ms on either side (0.022).

| 7–9 | pyramidal neurons; activity shimmers up their aligned apical dendrites | |
| 9–11 | a synapse on a dendritic spine: a vesicle fuses, transmitter crosses the cleft and binds | |

| 13–15 | the potential spreads down the dendrite; sink (cyan) at the synapse, source (amber) at the soma; the current loop; neighbours | |
| 15–17 | a population of aligned neurons fires in step; their small fields add into one | fields add up |
| 17–19 | the summed field pulses outward as contour ripples | |
| 19–21 | the ripples cross CSF, skull and scalp, widening and fading; a broad faint potential reaches the scalp | spreads to the scalp |

| 23–25 | one electrode cup on its gel: the potential under it, a tiny waveform on its lead | |
| 25–27 | a second electrode's lead joins: one differential channel outputs A − B | measures A − B |
| 27–29 | the weak signal, magnified: microvolts riding on mains hum and slow drift | microvolts |
| 29–31 | the differential amplifier: the difference grows tall | AMPLIFIER |
| 31–33 | the same hum on both inputs mostly cancels (a small residue stays) | shared noise cancels |
| 33–35 | a filter: drift and fast noise attenuated, the EEG band passes | |
| 35–37 | a sampling clock turns the analog voltage into digital values | sampled → digital |
| 37–39 | the multichannel recording: channels alike in some regions, different in others | |
| 39–41 | the patient at rest, eyes closed; posterior channels rhythmic | |

## How it is made

Built with the **huashu-art-motion** skill (`.claude/skills/huashu-art-motion`), open tier: the shot list
`镜头表.md` was written first and linted with `scripts/storyboard_lint.py`; the film runs on a copy of the skill's
Canvas engine (`scripts/engine`: segment table, transitions, `CAM` log-zoom camera, `MO` easings, `TOON`-style flat
shading) with the y1 Kurzgesagt grammar; `engine/render.py` is the skill's renderer (only change: BT.709 tags); QA used
`scripts/qa.py` and `scripts/film_gate.py`.

Seven segments (`engine/eras.js`) are joined by the engine's own transitions: lens reveals for the scale dives (into
the cortex, into a spine, into the O1 electrode), crossfades on pull-backs, and a match cut from the digital samples to
the monitor trace. Each segment's camera is computed from the film time alone, so transitions are drawn live (vector
redraw, never an enlarged bitmap). Every object is drawn in code as flat vector shapes with two-tone faceting (a shadow
band toward the lower right, a thin highlight toward the upper left), no outlines, soft radial glow only on electrical
signals. All randomness is seeded: the same t always draws the same frame (`qa.py` checks this per segment).

## Colour code

| colour | means |
|---|---|
| deep navy | the ground |
| coral pink | the brain and cortex (white matter paler) |
| soft lavender | neurons (pastel, low saturation) |
| bright cyan | electrical activity: pulses, currents, the field, sinks; the posterior EEG channels |
| warm yellow | synaptic activity: neurotransmitter |
| amber | current sources (opposite to the cyan sinks); mains hum; the eyes-open marker |
| silver and white | electrodes and leads; the clinician's coat |
| dark blue and teal | electronics: monitor, amplifier box, amplifier, filter and converter panels |
| cyan and soft green | the EEG waveforms (green = frontal/central channels, cyan = parietal/occipital) |

## The science (what the picture keeps honest)

- EEG records **differences in potential** between electrodes; routine scalp EEG **injects nothing** into the brain.
- The scalp signal mainly reflects **summed postsynaptic activity** of large populations of aligned, synchronized
  **pyramidal neurons**; single action potentials are not the dominant source (no "neurons as wires").
- The field spreads by **volume conduction** through brain, CSF, skull and scalp; the skull is not an insulator — the
  potential arrives widened and very small (microvolts).
- The electrode senses the potential through its gel; it does not extract electricity.
- The **differential amplifier** enlarges the A − B difference and rejects much — not all — of the shared interference;
  filters attenuate drift and fast noise and add no neural information; sampling turns the measured voltage into
  digital values.
- Eyes-closed **posterior alpha** is a normal finding; opening the eyes usually attenuates it; not every channel looks
  the same. EEG is not imaging (not CT, not MRI) and does not read thoughts; not every pattern is a seizure; a normal
  EEG does not exclude every disorder; responses vary between people. Colours and fields are explanatory graphics, not
  visible light. The waveforms are illustrative, not patient data. Time is compressed.

## Sound design

An original score, mixed low: gentle ambient pads, a subtle synth bass, soft electronic pulses, a sequencer of glassy
plucks that tightens to sixteenths in the machine section, minimal digital percussion. A four-note motif (F#–C#–E–A)
marks the hook, the signal reaching the electrodes, the machine and the alpha rhythm. During the eyes-closed scenes a
shimmer flutters at **10 Hz — the alpha frequency itself** — following the posterior alpha envelope, and stops when
the eyes open. All 111 SFX come from the same event table that drives the picture, and every event sits on the
sixteenth-note grid, so each sound lands on the beat: the hook pulse and waveform sweep, layer clicks, the dive, network
ticks, the transmitter release, ion pops, the dipole, synchronized rising tones, field ripples, layer thuds, electrode
ticks, measurement pulses, the amplification sweep, interference fading, a filter sweep, rapid sampling ticks,
recording pulses, the alpha texture, the eyes-open transition. No vocals, no drops.

## QA (numbers, not a viewing test)

- **Shot list** — `storyboard_lint`: yellow only (scenes 1–3 are 1 s each: the brief's hook timing).
- **Film gate** — `film_gate.py` on a 720×1280 / 30 fps proxy: **passed** — fast-motion frames 37.5 % (worst 28 s
  window 18.6 %), no blank frames, blue-purple frames 0.0 %, 14 shots. One yellow: 16.4 push-ins per minute (15 in the
  film, 2 of them within 0.5 s), balanced by pull-backs (push-ins are 56 % of push/pull events) — the film is built on
  scale travel (pushing through an object into the next world), and after each dive the camera comes back out.
- **Engine QA** — `qa.py --project engine`: all 7 segments deterministic (two renders of the same t identical pixel
  for pixel), no hard jumps, at most 4 % still frame pairs in any segment, text inside the frame and out of the subtitle band; 10–51 ms per frame
  on average (peak 117 ms); every transition smoke-tested.
- **Loop** — above (three repetitions of the proxy, and the WAVs).
- **Sync** — `node tools/sync_qa.js`: 111 event times, all on the sixteenth-note grid; all 111 SFX start on their
  event; the picture shows each event on the nearest frame (at most half a frame, 8.3 ms, from the beat); 67 percussive
  onsets measured on the SFX stem: median 0.56 ms, max 2.5 ms from their event.
- **Audio** — `node tools/audio_qa.js`: 107 of 111 cues are within 6 dB of the music or louder in their strongest octave
  band; the other four are deliberately soft (the eye-close breath, two camera whooshes, the riser under the last bars).

## Self-review against the skill's six failure modes

1. **Slide-deck feel** — no page frame or bullet text; one picture event per micro-scene; camera moves vary (pull-back,
   push, pan, dive, settle) and come back out after going in; the end is an action on the main object (the camera
   settling on the trace), not a closing card.
2. **Copying a demo** — composition, characters and objects are new and built for this subject (no demo layouts).
3. **No concrete object** — every row of the shot list names a concrete object and what it does.
4. **Dead background / empty frame** — the subject fills the frame; backgrounds change with the world and keep a slow
   parallax drift; no blank frames (film gate).
5. **Real material drawn in code** — none was supplied; the EEG is an illustrative model.
6. **AI look** — one style, one palette (no blue-purple gradients, no neon, no bloom); the patient is a proportioned
   side profile whose only facial detail is the eyelid (the subject of the alpha response), the clinician is seen only
   from behind; no faces on molecules.

No separate reviewer agent was used. The physiology follows standard descriptions of EEG generation and recording;
specific numbers in the notes were not re-checked against online sources.
